---
title: Title Blocks
---

## Overview

HTML pages rendered with Quarto include a formatted title block at the start of the article. The title block gathers metadata from the document front matter — the title, subtitle, authors and their affiliations, publication and modification dates, DOI, abstract, description, keywords, and category labels — and lays it out in stylized groups.

For example, this front matter:

``` yaml
---
title: Summarizing Output for Reproducible Documents
description: A summary of best practices
author:
  - name: Norah Jones
    affiliations:
      - name: Spacely Sprockets
date: 2018-05-04
---
```

produces a title block with the title and description at the top, followed by a metadata grid with the author, affiliation, and publication date.

The title block lays out these elements automatically. If you'd like, you can control its behavior using `title-block-style`. Three options are available:

-   `default` — The default treatment gathers the title elements into stylized groups and styles them with a smaller font face.

-   `plain` — The plain treatment does all of the title element processing (gathering and organizing the elements) but does not apply the default title block styling.

-   `none` — `none` disables title block processing altogether. The title block is emitted in Pandoc's plain form: an unstyled header containing the title, authors, date, and abstract.

::: callout-note
Quarto 1's fourth style, `manuscript`, is not currently supported. Documents that specify it fall back to `default`.
:::

## Authors and Affiliations

Authors may be written as simple names or as structured records. A structured author can carry an ORCID, an email address, a homepage URL, academic degrees, and one or more affiliations:

``` yaml
---
author:
  - name: Norah Jones
    orcid: 0000-0002-1825-0097
    email: norah@example.com
    url: https://example.com/norah
    degrees:
      - PhD
    affiliations:
      - name: Carnegie Mellon University
        department: School of Music
---
```

When any author has an affiliation, the title block renders authors and affiliations side by side in a two-column grid. Author names link to their `url`, and email and ORCID entries render as icon links after the name.

Affiliations may also be declared once at the top level and referenced by id, which keeps the front matter compact when several authors share an institution:

``` yaml
---
author:
  - name: Norah Jones
    affiliations:
      - ref: cmu
  - name: Bill Malone
    affiliations:
      - ref: cmu
affiliations:
  - id: cmu
    name: Carnegie Mellon University
---
```

## Title Banners

If you'd like a more prominent title block, you can use `title-block-banner` to create a banner style title block. A banner positions the title, subtitle, description, and categories in a full-width band above the article, with the remaining metadata below it. For example:

``` yaml
---
title-block-banner: true
---
```

In this case, the color of the banner is determined by the document theme.

### Custom Backgrounds

You can control the banner background by providing either a CSS color (e.g. `"#FFDDFF"` or `red`) or the path to an image, which becomes the banner's background. For example, to use a banner image you might write:

``` yaml
---
title-block-banner: images/banner.jpeg
---
```

The image is copied into the output directory automatically.

### Foreground Color

You can also specify the color of the banner's text, using `title-block-banner-color` and providing a CSS color. The special values `body` and `body-bg` select the theme's body text color and body background color, respectively.

## Categories

When the front matter lists `categories`, the title block renders them as labeled chips under the title (inside the banner, when a banner is active). To suppress the chips while keeping the categories available to listings, set:

``` yaml
---
title-block-categories: false
---
```

## Date

Quarto includes the document's `date` (and `date-modified`, when present) in the title block. In addition to writing a standard date, you may use a few special keywords that generate the date for you: `today` provides the current date with the time set to 0, `now` provides the current date and time, and `last-modified` provides the modification date and time of the document file itself.

### Formatting

When the title block uses the `default` or `plain` styles, Quarto formats the date in a readable long form (e.g. "May 4, 2018"). You can control the formatting by specifying a `date-format` in the document front matter. For example:

``` yaml
---
title: Summarizing Output for Reproducible Documents
date: 2018-05-04
date-format: short
---
```

For the available named styles and format strings, see the [date format reference](dates.qmd).

## Metadata Labels

The metadata labels in the title block ("Author", "Published", and so on) have default values that you may want to replace with your own. The following options customize them:

| Option              | Default label            |
|---------------------|--------------------------|
| `author-title`      | Author / Authors         |
| `affiliation-title` | Affiliation / Affiliations |
| `published-title`   | Published                |
| `modified-title`    | Modified                 |
| `abstract-title`    | Abstract                 |
| `description-title` | Description              |
| `doi-title`         | Doi                      |

The author and affiliation labels pluralize automatically, according to how many authors and affiliations the document declares.

::: callout-note
Label defaults are currently English-only. Localized labels (Quarto 1's `lang`-based label system) are planned as part of a broader localization effort.
:::

## Custom Title Blocks

To replace the built-in title block entirely, provide your own version of the `title-block.html` template partial via `template-partials`. Quarto 2 uses the same partial names as Quarto 1 (`title-block.html`, `title-metadata.html`, `_title-meta-author.html`), so partials written for Quarto 1 continue to work. See [Templates](templates.qmd) for details.
